improvements.hypothesis: Putting the ticket ID in every agent label lets org/spend.mjs attribute 100% of spend automatically
Linking architecture/core-runtime-api.md and modules.md in every build ticket removes cross-team interface mismatches
improvements.note: Core API doc helped module code (no ctx misuse found), but 6 contract gaps between openapi and core still surfaced. Replaced by IMP-5.

improvements.hypothesis: Running 3 workflows side by side (6 agents) instead of 2 raises throughput without raising cost per point
improvements.note: 166 pts in ~26 min agent wall-clock ≈ 383 pts/h vs Sprint 0 ~190 pts/h; cost per point $0.12 vs $0.06 (bigger tickets, more review)

improvements.hypothesis: Reviewers of pipeline tickets also run tests/e2e and tests/security, so cross-module defects are caught before acceptance
improvements.metric: defects found after acceptance per sprint
improvements.note: No defects found after acceptance for Sprint 2 pipeline tickets so far; the 11 found this sprint were Sprint 1 escapes

improvements.hypothesis: An architecture-hub triage agent at sprint start answers every open contract-change request, so no request waits a full sprint
improvements.metric: open contract-change requests at sprint close
improvements.note: 25/25 contract-change messages answered within the sprint

improvements.hypothesis: UI tickets include a Playwright smoke test in real Chromium, raising first-pass acceptance for Experience from 0.75
improvements.note: Experience first-pass acceptance 3/3 with Playwright gate; also caught 4 escaped Sprint 1 defects

improvements.hypothesis: Reviewers must record the verdict themselves; the workflow script also records it from the structured verdict when missing
improvements.metric: tickets with structured verdict but no fabric review
improvements.note: One verdict still unrecorded after a security rework reset the status; orchestrator close step now reconciles structured verdicts with the fabric

improvements.hypothesis: Contract-version-sensitive tests read the version from openapi.yaml instead of hard-coding it, so contract bumps do not break other teams
improvements.metric: tests broken by a contract bump
improvements.note: Contract bump in S3-SEC-01 broke no other tests

improvements.hypothesis: A security reviewer agent runs on every module ticket at mid tier, cutting security escapes to zero
improvements.metric: high security findings discovered after acceptance
improvements.note: Gate found 1 high + 5 mediums on 5 module tickets; the high was fixed before close. Cost ~$0.25 per gated ticket.

improvements.hypothesis: ic-experience-claimant-web-dev config had 3 escaped defects (diagnosis: missing context, UI never run in a browser, not a capability limit). Intervention #1, fix the ticket/context: the Playwright UI gate (IMP-6) applies to its Sprint 3 rework ticket
improvements.note: Claimant web dev configuration: 0 new escaped defects with the Playwright context; no further intervention needed

improvements.hypothesis: Rehearsing the demo (and any end-user walkthrough) against the running system is a standing ticket every sprint from Sprint 2 on, so product gaps surface a sprint earlier
improvements.metric: product gaps found in the final sprint
improvements.note: Not measurable inside this PoC (no further sprint); playbook updated so rehearsal is a standing ticket from Sprint 2

improvements.hypothesis: Two bottom-10% configurations (PI-1, PI-2) were diagnosed as dependency/context problems, not capability; interventions are context fixes, not tier changes or retirement
improvements.metric: first-pass acceptance of the two configurations
improvements.note: Recorded in org/scorecards/interventions.json | S5 measurement recorded at sprint close
improvements.result: PI-2 1/1 first pass in S5 (low confidence); PI-1 not re-measured (no ticket); new PI-3 traced to orchestrator ticket scoping, so the same context-fix approach extends to the orchestrator via IMP-14

improvements.hypothesis: Running the full suite (tests/ui, tests/integration) in every review of a src/ change stops UI regressions from escaping acceptance
improvements.metric: escaped defects found in tests/ui after acceptance, per sprint

improvements.hypothesis: Listing every test that encodes the behaviour being changed in the ticket paths removes scope-caused rework
improvements.metric: rework rounds caused by out-of-scope tests, per sprint
improvements.implementation: standards v3 ticket scoping rule; orchestrator greps tests/ before dispatch

improvements.hypothesis: Path-only commits, no stash/checkout during workflows, and image builds from a clean worktree remove orchestrator-caused incidents
improvements.metric: incidents caused by orchestrator git operations, per sprint
improvements.implementation: standards v3; deploy runbook deployment log; adopted for the 04:18 deploy

sprintReviews.name: Sprint 6: production-grade experience
sprintReviews.goal: Sponsor feedback: the UI must look and feel like a production application, with a demo persona switcher. Design system and shell, persona switcher, four app redesigns reviewed on screenshots, redeploy.

sprintReviews.name: Sprint 5: production-path credibility
sprintReviews.goal: Verified live deployment, live-model evaluation, 0 open medium security findings, spikes for the four production gaps

shipped: Deployed web apps work behind IAP (runtime dev flag, X-Fnol-Authorization); 3 redeploys logged in docs/deploy-fnol-poc.md
Policy-number oracle closed: last name + ZIP holder check, per-policy atomic lockout, agent-producer rule
One safe-pattern checker for tenant regexes at save and evaluation; AI output validation, tenant attribution, untrusted-input framing, labelled-name redaction
Security re-review closed 12 findings with real tests: 0 high, 1 medium (SEC2-011 residual), 7 low open
First live Gemini evaluation (640 calls, $0.59 GCP, 0 redaction leaks) and per-task model selection: local rules primary except subrogation on gemini-2.5-flash
Four production spikes (Cloud SQL store port, OIDC verifier, Pub/Sub outbox, KMS envelope) as design + tested proof
Demo test runs against a remote URL; golden sets at 20 cases per task (5 adversarial)
risks: SEC2-011 residual: lowercase, accented and unlisted-label names still reach cloud models
R2: devMode on in the IAP-only deployment (accepted PoC risk, Sprint 6)
Claude on Vertex not evaluated: quota 0 until the sponsor enables Model Garden
Intermittent CSR UI test under full-suite load (S5-QE-03 carried over); quality.json shows 1 failure
Remote demo against the deployed URL not run: needs an IAP token, blocked by session permissions

gcpUsd.note: Vertex AI spend billed to the sponsor GCP project, outside the $250 agent budget

went_well: Council caught real plan defects before any build (file overlaps, cost cap, IAP grant scope, R2 sequencing)
19 of 22 first-pass in waves 1-2; security gate found 4 mediums that became same-sprint fixes
The live eval paid for itself on its first run: a real redaction leak and a harness bug, both fixed and re-run the same sprint
The sponsor-reported outage was root-caused from logs without guesswork and fixed within one wave
went_badly: The review gate ran only e2e+security, so a UI regression escaped (DEF-001) and reached the sponsor
Orchestrator ticket scoping caused 3 rework rounds and one design defect (token-name identity)
Orchestrator ran git stash during a workflow (incident, no loss)
Quality report script passes a directory to node --test and always reports 1 failing test
manager_retros: workflow: identity checks need a product decision before code; last name + ZIP should have been the first design
ai: tests with fakes must be as strict as the real provider contract (schema-sensitive fakes)
quality: an intermittent UI test needs a trace, not reruns

shipped: UI-entered claims verify coverage and fast-track (intake-to-claim mapping, insured-vehicle pick from policy)

Demo script automated: 6/6 beats pass
COTS readiness, demo script and configuration guide refreshed
risks: Open: SEC medium/low findings (see architecture/security-review-s2.md), policy-vehicles policy-number oracle (medium)

went_well: Every demo gap found in Sprint 3 is closed and proved by an automated demo test
Security gate caught a high in an untouched Sprint 1 file while reviewing a neighbour, before release
Pre-planned ticket mode let the orchestrator dispatch follow-ups without manager overhead
went_badly: 5 more Sprint 0-1 escapes surfaced (product gaps found only by rehearsal); IMP-11 is the fix

Demo data on first start; configuration guide, 10-minute demo script, COTS readiness assessment, docs index

went_well: Security gate found a high the acceptance reviewer missed, and the rework loop fixed it in-sprint

went_badly: A correct fix (estimate totals) regressed severity calibration because AI tiers and triage tiers are duplicated across team boundaries

Sprint 3 needed an orchestrator-dispatched follow-up wave

quality: DoD test needed GET /claims after submit because submit returns a summary; contract says full Claim

Adjuster first view and carrier admin console; Playwright smoke tests for all four apps

risks: 7 high security findings open (tracked as todo tests)

went_well: Integration squad (single strong-tier owner) fixed 54 e2e failures in one ticket: one owner for cross-module behaviour works
